html:
SMTO-EXE-0115 — SMTO can't find that item on the page or in downloads

GUID: 1e07b5e2-7633-51e8-a1d1-188ef08ec603
Slug: browser-element-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO looked for a button, field, link or downloaded file, but nothing matching was there. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO: "Look at the page again and tell me what buttons and fields you can see." SMTO then works from what is on the page now instead of a guessed name.
  2. If the item only appears after something else, such as opening a menu, scrolling or the page finishing loading, ask SMTO to do that first. SMTO only finds items that are visible on the page at that moment.
  3. Tell SMTO the exact words shown on the button or next to the field you mean. SMTO matches items by their visible label, so the exact wording helps it find the right one.
  4. For a downloaded file, ask SMTO to list the downloads in its browser and use one from that list. SMTO only knows about downloads that happened in this browser while it was working, and they are lost when the browser closes.

What success looks like

  • SMTO names the item it found on the page or in its downloads list and continues the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with a description of the item you wanted, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't tell SMTO to click something that only looks similar; it could press the wrong button. Items inside boxes embedded from another site can't be used by SMTO's browser.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The browser locator matched no visible element on the page, or the requested download_id/after_download_id is not among the session's tracked downloads.

What this means

  • A semantic locator produced no matching element, or an explicitly requested download ID was absent from the session's retained downloads. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • A semantic locator produced no matching element, or an explicitly requested download ID was absent from the session's retained downloads.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish element lookup from download lookup, then inspect a fresh snapshot/find result or download list in the same session.

How to fix it

  • PlaywrightBackend._target raises element_not_found when the semantic locator returns zero matches (only visible elements count unless visible_only=false); _downloads raises it when download_id or after_download_id is absent from session.downloads. Take a fresh browser.snapshot or browser.find and use an exact returned element_ref, or call browser.downloads and use a returned download_id. Locators search the main frame only, so iframe content is not matched.
  • Take a new snapshot/find or list downloads and use the returned exact identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Take a new snapshot/find or list downloads and use the returned exact identity.

How to verify the fix

  • An exact current element or retained download is selected for the intended operation.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
